questions.question_text: Two compounds have the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements and properties. This phenomenon is called
questions.explanation: Structural isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how atoms are connected, which can produce different properties.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Carbon and its Compounds, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which pair represents structural isomers with molecular formula C₄H₁₀?
questions.explanation: Butane has two structural arrangements: straight-chain n-butane and branched 2-methylpropane (isobutane), both C₄H₁₀.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: When methane reacts with chlorine in sunlight, one hydrogen atom can be replaced by chlorine. This reaction is classified as
questions.explanation: In photochemical chlorination of methane, a chlorine atom substitutes for a hydrogen atom, producing chloromethane and hydrogen chloride.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Carbon and its Compounds, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A sample decolourises bromine water without heating or a catalyst. Which inference is most consistent with a carbon-carbon multiple bond?
questions.option_a: An unsaturated compound has undergone addition
questions.option_b: A saturated alkane has undergone neutralisation
questions.option_d: An alcohol has undergone fermentation only
questions.explanation: Bromine water can be decolourised by addition across carbon-carbon double or triple bonds, indicating unsaturation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Carbon and its Compounds, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Ethene is converted into ethane by adding hydrogen in the presence of a catalyst. The change is an example of
questions.explanation: Hydrogenation adds hydrogen across the C=C bond of ethene to form ethane; suitable metal catalysts are used.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Carbon and its Compounds, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The black powder added to rubber to improve its strength and wear resistance is commonly
questions.explanation: Carbon black acts as a reinforcing filler in rubber products such as tyres, improving strength and abrasion resistance.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A molecule contains a carbonyl group at the end of its carbon chain. Which functional group is indicated?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes contain a terminal carbonyl group (–CHO); ketones have a carbonyl carbon within the carbon chain.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which feature distinguishes a ketone from an aldehyde in a simple open-chain molecule?
questions.option_a: Its carbonyl carbon is bonded to carbon groups on both sides
questions.option_b: It must contain a carbon-carbon triple bond
questions.option_c: Its carbonyl group is at the terminal carbon as –CHO
questions.explanation: Ketones have an internal carbonyl carbon bonded to two carbon groups; aldehydes have a terminal –CHO group.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Ethanol is oxidised by a suitable oxidising agent to form which common carboxylic acid?
questions.explanation: Oxidation of ethanol can produce ethanoic acid; vinegar contains dilute ethanoic acid.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Carbon and its Compounds, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Ethanol reacts with sodium metal, releasing a gas. Which gas is evolved?
questions.explanation: Sodium reacts with the hydrogen of ethanol's hydroxyl group to form sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Carbon and its Compounds, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Ethanol and ethanoic acid are warmed with concentrated sulphuric acid. The sweet-smelling product is generally an
questions.explanation: Esterification combines an alcohol and carboxylic acid to form an ester and water; many esters have fruity odours.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Carbon and its Compounds, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Hydrolysis of an ester with a strong alkali produces an alcohol and the salt of a carboxylic acid. In soap manufacture, this process is called
questions.explanation: Saponification is alkaline hydrolysis of fats or oils, producing glycerol and salts of fatty acids (soap).
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Carbon and its Compounds, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why does soap form scum and clean less effectively in hard water?
questions.option_a: Calcium and magnesium ions form insoluble salts with soap
questions.option_b: Hard water removes every carbon atom from soap
questions.option_d: Hard water contains no dissolved ions
questions.explanation: Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ react with soap anions to form insoluble precipitates, consuming soap and producing scum.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Carbon and its Compounds, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Synthetic detergents often clean effectively in hard water because their calcium and magnesium salts are generally
questions.option_a: more soluble than the corresponding soap scum
questions.explanation: Many detergents do not form insoluble precipitates with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ as readily as ordinary soaps, so they remain effective in hard water.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Carbon and its Compounds, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In water, soap molecules can cluster with hydrocarbon tails directed inward and ionic ends toward water. Such a cluster is a
questions.explanation: Micelles have hydrophobic tails aggregated inward around oily dirt and hydrophilic ionic ends facing the surrounding water.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Carbon and its Compounds, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Most simple covalent compounds have relatively low melting points and conduct electricity poorly because they usually
questions.option_a: consist of neutral molecules with no freely mobile ions or electrons
questions.option_b: contain a sea of mobile electrons
questions.option_c: are made only of metal cations
questions.explanation: Many molecular covalent substances lack mobile charge carriers, and the forces between molecules are relatively weak; network covalent solids are important exceptions.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Many non-polar hydrocarbon compounds mix poorly with water but dissolve in non-polar organic solvents. This behaviour follows the principle that
questions.option_a: substances with similar intermolecular character tend to mix
questions.option_b: all covalent compounds dissolve in water
questions.option_c: ionic solids are always soluble in oil
questions.explanation: Non-polar hydrocarbons interact weakly with polar water but are more compatible with non-polar solvents; actual solubility depends on molecular structure.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: When ethene molecules join repeatedly to form polyethene, the process is
questions.explanation: Many ethene molecules add across their double bonds to form the long-chain polymer polyethene without eliminating a small molecule.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The monomer used to make polyvinyl chloride (PVC) is
questions.explanation: PVC is formed by addition polymerisation of chloroethene, commonly called vinyl chloride.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which polymer is made from tetrafluoroethene and is noted for chemical resistance and a low-friction surface?
questions.explanation: Tetrafluoroethene polymerises to PTFE, known for chemical resistance and non-stick, low-friction uses.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: When a carbon fuel burns with an inadequate oxygen supply, which poisonous gas can be produced by incomplete combustion?
questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion can produce carbon monoxide, which binds haemoglobin strongly and interferes with oxygen transport.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT science references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Solid carbon dioxide used as a refrigerant is commonly called
questions.explanation: Solid CO₂ is known as dry ice; it sublimes under ordinary atmospheric pressure rather than melting into a liquid.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT science references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A smoky yellow flame from a carbon-rich fuel generally indicates
questions.option_a: incomplete combustion and incandescent soot particles
questions.option_c: absence of carbon in the fuel
questions.explanation: A luminous yellow flame often results from tiny hot carbon particles when combustion is incomplete; sufficient oxygen usually gives a cleaner blue flame.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT science references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which formula is the general molecular formula for an open-chain alkyne containing one carbon-carbon triple bond?
questions.explanation: An acyclic monoalkyne has two fewer hydrogen atoms than the corresponding alkene and follows CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (for n ≥ 2).
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: How many carbon-carbon sigma and pi bonds occur in an isolated carbon-carbon triple bond?
questions.explanation: A triple bond contains one sigma bond and two pi bonds formed by sideways overlap.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which atmospheric process is enhanced by increasing carbon dioxide concentration and contributes to warming near Earth’s surface?
questions.option_a: Absorption and re-emission of outgoing infrared radiation
questions.option_b: Reflection of all incoming visible light
questions.explanation: CO₂ is a greenhouse gas that absorbs infrared radiation, contributing to the greenhouse effect.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Carbon and its Compounds, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The natural polymer in rubber latex is composed mainly of repeating units of
questions.explanation: Natural rubber consists mainly of cis-1,4-polyisoprene, a polymer of isoprene units.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which product forms when ethanol is oxidised incompletely under controlled conditions rather than all the way to carbon dioxide and water?
questions.explanation: Controlled oxidation of ethanol can produce ethanal; stronger or continued oxidation can yield ethanoic acid.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which of these is the principal hydrocarbon in compressed natural gas (CNG)?
questions.explanation: CNG consists chiefly of methane, though its exact composition can vary by source and processing.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which pair lists the principal hydrocarbons commonly present in liquefied petroleum gas (LPG)?
questions.explanation: LPG is composed mainly of propane and butane in proportions that vary by market and season.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In alcoholic fermentation, yeast converts glucose chiefly into
questions.explanation: Yeast fermentation of glucose produces ethanol and carbon dioxide under anaerobic conditions.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry and biology references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which carbon compound is used as a common solvent and fuel, and is toxic if ingested because metabolism can damage the optic nerve?
questions.explanation: Methanol is toxic; its metabolites, including formate, can cause severe metabolic acidosis and optic nerve injury.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The carbon atoms in a benzene ring are arranged in which basic structural pattern?
questions.option_a: A six-membered ring with delocalised electrons
questions.option_b: A straight chain with six isolated ions
questions.option_c: A tetrahedral cluster with no bonds
questions.option_d: A four-membered ring containing only oxygen
questions.explanation: Benzene has a six-carbon ring with delocalised pi electrons; its bonding is not well represented by a single fixed alternating-bond structure.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
